lead: Before the bot, you’ll see the whole idea in a short script from the jornada-agentes repository: four folders, one task at a time, resume after Ctrl+C, and failures kept separate with the reason.
objetivo: run the homegrown queue, interrupt it halfway through, and explain why the second run doesn’t redo what’s already done.
hero_alt: Notebook with a dark terminal beside four paper folders on a desk.

aprende.t: The four folders and a task’s path
Switch the engine: claude or codex

secoes.sub: Each request is a .md file that moves between folders.

nos.detalhe: Each .md file is a request, written the way you’d write it in chat. The order follows the file names.
The script moves the file here before calling the agent. If you press Ctrl+C or the computer crashes, it stays here, which makes it possible to resume.
It worked (exit code 0 and a non-empty response): the final file contains the request, a line with ---, and the agent’s response.
It failed or the response was empty: the file goes here with the exit code and what the agent printed. The queue moves on to the next task.

secoes.volta: When you run it again: rodando/ → entrada/
secoes.legenda: Click each folder. The key is rodando/: the task only leaves that folder when it finishes, moving to feito/ or falhou/.

rolagem_fim.titulo: Running it again only picks up what’s left
rolagem_fim.texto: At startup, the script returns anything left in rodando/ to entrada/. Anything already in feito/ is never redone.

secoes.sub: Run it, interrupt it halfway through with the Ctrl+C button, then run it again.

msg.inicio: 5 tasks in entrada/. Click “Run the queue”.
msg.rodando: Running: one task at a time, from entrada/ to rodando/ and then feito/ or falhou/.
msg.parou: Interrupted. The task in progress stayed in rodando/. Run it again to see the resume.
msg.retoma: Resumed: what was in rodando/ went back to entrada/. What was already in feito/ is not redone.
msg.fim: Queue empty: everything is in feito/.
msg.fimfalha: Queue empty. One task went to falhou/ with this reason: that’s what you check in the morning.

secoes.legenda: Illustrative browser simulation: the tasks don’t actually run. The failure is intentional, to show the falhou/ folder.

secoes.titulo: The script and how to use it
secoes.sub: It’s in ferramentas/fila-caseira.sh in the jornada-agentes repository. Both engines run through your subscription.

blocos.conteudo:
git clone https://github.com/inematds/jornada-agentes.git
cd jornada-agentes
mkdir -p fila/entrada
echo "Summarize in 5 lines what a task queue is." > fila/entrada/01.md
echo "List 3 risks of leaving an agent running on its own." > fila/entrada/02.md
./ferramentas/fila-caseira.sh fila          # default engine: claude
./ferramentas/fila-caseira.sh fila codex    # or codex

mkdir -p "$PASTA/entrada" "$PASTA/rodando" "$PASTA/feito" "$PASTA/falhou"

# resume: anything left in "rodando" (crash, Ctrl+C) goes back to the queue
for f in "$PASTA"/rodando/*.md; do [ -e "$f" ] && mv "$f" "$PASTA/entrada/"; done

for f in "$PASTA"/entrada/*.md; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || { echo "empty queue"; break; }
  nome=$(basename "$f")
  mv "$f" "$PASTA/rodando/$nome"          # picks up the task (only one at a time)
  saida=$(claude -p "$(cat "$PASTA/rodando/$nome")" < /dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ $rc -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$saida" ]; then
    # request + --- + response go to feito/
  else
    # request + ERROR (rc) + output go to falhou/
  fi
done

abas.html:
1. Creates the four folders (running it again won’t break anything).
  2. Returns anything left in rodando/ to entrada/.
  3. Picks up one file at a time and moves it to rodando/ before calling the agent.
  4. Exit code 0 and a non-empty response: feito/. Otherwise: falhou/ with the exit code.
  5. At the end, counts how many are in each folder.

abas.rot: What the bot does in addition
abas.html:
• Receives requests through Telegram, not just from files.
  • Five queues with different limits, and automatic retries.
  • A deadline for each task and a chat notification when it’s done.
  • An approval gate in the middle of flows.

secoes.sub: Use two tasks from your queue on paper (lesson 2).

exercicios.titulo: E2 · A homemade queue in 30 lines
exercicios.texto: Create two or three tasks in fila/entrada and run fila-caseira.sh. In a second run, interrupt with Ctrl+C while a task is in rodando/, check the folder, and run it again.
exercicios.pronto: the tasks are in fila/feito with their responses, and you saw the queue continue where it left off after Ctrl+C.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: You interrupted the queue in the middle of a task. What happens when you run it again?
opcoes: Everything starts over from the beginning.
The interrupted task goes back to entrada/ and the queue continues with what’s left.
The queue only starts working again the next day.
perguntas.explica: That’s what makes it a durable queue: anything left in rodando/ goes back to entrada/, and anything already in feito/ isn’t redone.

perguntas.p: Why does the script move the file to rodando/ BEFORE calling the agent?
opcoes: So the agent can read it faster.
To mark which task is in progress; if there’s a crash, it stays there and gets picked up again.
To hide the task from you.
Because the agent only reads files in that folder.
perguntas.explica: Moving it first is the record that says, “I’m working on this.” It’s the homemade version of inemaccbot’s lease.

perguntas.p: The agent responded, but the response was empty. Where does the task go?
opcoes: feito/, because there was no error.
falhou/, because an empty response also counts as a failure.
perguntas.explica: The script requires exit code 0 AND a non-empty response. Without a response, there’s nothing to check, so it’s a failure.
